name: 173. A caller's key pin on the routed provider keeps a session from moving the request (session-caller-pin)
description:
A key the caller pins (x-bf-api-key-id or x-bf-api-key) belongs to one provider. When that provider heads the routed chain, a session used to reorder the request onto the provider it was bound to anyway, carrying the pin to a provider with no such key: that attempt failed at key selection, the fallback cleared the pin, and the request was served on a key the caller never chose. The session now leaves the chain alone when the caller pinned one of the head provider's keys, as it already does for a provider-prefixed model. A pin on another provider's key, and a direct key, still leave the session to decide.

Each row builds two run-scoped OpenAI-backed providers and a header-gated rule targeting P1 with P2 as its fallback, then binds a session to P2 by having P1 refuse its keys. (1) P1's keys are repaired and the request pins P1's weight-0 key 1: P1 must serve on key 1 as the primary. Before the change the session promoted P2, the pin failed there, and P1 served as a fallback on key 1b. (2) The request pins P2's weight-0 key 2p: the session still promotes P2, which serves on key 2p as the primary. Each row deletes what it made. Run with FEATURE="session-caller-pin".

var j = null; if (!err && res.code === 200) { try { j = res.json(); } catch (e) { j = null; } }
pm.test('the trail says the caller\u2019s pin on P1 keeps the routing decision, so the session does not move the request', function () {
pm.expect(String(j.routing_engine_logs || '')).to.include("Request pins the caller's key on " + state.p1 + ', so the session keeps the routing decision for gpt-4o-mini');
// An unpinned turn of the same session: the binding to P2 is unchanged, so the session moves P2 first.

pm.expect(ri2.is_fallback === true, 'P2 served as the primary: ' + (res ? res.text() : '')).to.eql(false);
